strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Elementwise Fusion
strategies.desc: Perform 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local elementwise scale/unscale operations fused between collectives. Each all-reduce dispatches once (8 total dispatches) on the full W*S tensor. Minimizes dispatch overhead by fusing all local operations (scale, divide, clone) into single kernels between collectives.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with reduce-scatter (producing S-sized local shard) followed by all-gather (reconstructing W*S tensor). This doubles dispatch count to 16 but reduces per-rank communication volume in the reduce-scatter phase. Trades more dispatches for better network bandwidth utilization at scale 224.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Exploit multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce followed by inter-node all-reduce for each of the 8 stages (16 total dispatches). At world size 224, assumes node-level grouping to reduce cross-node traffic. Optimizes for NUMA/network hierarchy but requires explicit node-aware rank grouping.

strategies.name: Batched Multi-Stage All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Concatenate operations from multiple stages and issue fewer, larger all-reduce calls on expanded tensors (e.g., 4 all-reduces each handling 2 stages' worth of data). Requires careful buffering of intermediate results but reduces dispatch count from 8 to 4. Trades memory footprint for fewer kernel launches.

strategies.name: In-Place Ring All-Reduce with Manual Chunking
strategies.desc:
Implement custom ring all-reduce pattern using point-to-point send/recv operations, processing W chunks sequentially in W-1 scatter-reduce and W-1 all-gather steps per stage (≈1800 dispatches total). Maximizes pipelining and overlap opportunities but dramatically increases dispatch count; only beneficial if dispatch overhead is negligible compared to computation latency.
